# Hash-pinned install set for the Sync Daemon E2E Tests job.
#
# Direct requirements: flask waitress cryptography cffi duckdb
#                      websocket-client truststore certifi
#
# Used by sync-test.yml's one job. That job was installing with a bare
# `pip install -e .`, which is the only install line left in this repo's CI
# with no pinned environment around it at all -- not even the pip bootstrap
# every other job starts from. So the entire runtime closure that setup.py
# declares resolved to whatever the index served that minute, on all six
# cells of its matrix, in the job that guards the cloud sync daemon.
#
# That matters more here than the unpinned-resolve argument usually does.
# This job's ten tests are almost all import-and-call assertions against
# `clawmetry.sync` -- encrypt/decrypt roundtrip, state roundtrip,
# detect_paths, load_config's FileNotFoundError. Every one of them runs
# through cryptography, cffi and duckdb. When one of those moves underneath
# the job, a red run is indistinguishable from a real regression in sync.py,
# which is the single thing this workflow exists to tell you.
#
# The eight names above are the dashboard's own runtime dependencies as
# setup.py declares them on this matrix's interpreters, so this set is the
# closure of `pip install -e .` rather than a per-workflow invention. It was
# read off a resolve, not assembled by hand: `pip install --dry-run --report`
# on CPython 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13 returns the SAME fifteen distributions at
# the same versions, which is why one file covers all three legs.
#
# `-e .` itself stays unpinned and is installed after this file with
# `--no-deps`. It is this repo's working tree -- the code under test -- and
# pinning it is precisely what the job exists to avoid. This file is the
# environment AROUND the code, never the code.
#
# Installed with `pip install --require-hashes`, which refuses to install
# anything not listed here with a matching hash -- so the job gets the exact
# artifacts this file names, or it fails. Every transitive dependency is
# present because --require-hashes demands the whole closure; that is the
# point, not padding.
#
# Each version lists the sha256 of EVERY distribution PyPI publishes for it
# (wheels for each platform, plus the sdist). pip accepts a download that
# matches any one of them, so the pin does not quietly depend on the runner
# resolving to the same wheel this file was generated against.
#
# SCOPE -- this file is CPython 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13, on ubuntu-latest and
# macos-latest, which is exactly sync-test.yml's matrix. It is deliberately
# NOT interchangeable with the other sets in this directory: cffi and
# cryptography are version-ceilinged by the interpreter (see CLAUDE.md
# "Dependencies"), and the `cffi<2` / `cryptography>=46,<50` band that
# applies below Python 3.10 resolves to different versions than the ones
# here. Every leg of this matrix is 3.11 or newer, so the whole matrix sits
# in one band and one file is correct for it. Do not reuse this file for a
# py3.9 job, and do not add a py3.9 leg to this matrix without splitting it.
#
# Because `-e .` is installed with `--no-deps`, this file is responsible for
# setup.py's whole declared runtime closure on those interpreters: if
# `install_requires` gains a dependency and this file does not, the job gets
# an environment missing it. The job fails loudly in that case rather than
# passing on a gap -- its first two steps import `clawmetry.sync` and
# `clawmetry.cli`, neither of which survives a missing runtime dependency.
#
# Updating: Dependabot owns the routine bumps and rewrites the hashes along
# with the version, so a bump arrives already verifiable. A pin with no
# updater is the frozen end of the same problem an unpinned install is at
# the other end of. The updater is the `/.github/requirements` pip entry in
# .github/dependabot.yml, whose group pattern is `*` and so covers this file.
#
# Generated from a `pip install --dry-run --report` resolve of `-e .`; the
# hashes are every sha256 PyPI publishes for each resolved version.
